brief: Something to keep my sewing supplies tidy.

requirements.requirement: Holds sewing supplies in separate open compartments (bins) so small items stay sorted.
requirements.evidence: Two hex bases (piece:0,0,0 and piece:1,0,0), each with a 2-compartment full-depth bin (bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2), joined by a joint bolt. Four open compartments in total.

requirements.requirement: Has at least one drawer so small items such as needles and buttons can be kept out of sight.
requirements.evidence: No drawer offers appeared on any half base I tried (half-e beside a full base, and alone). No drawer was added.

requirements.requirement: Stays a compact desk-size organiser, not a large unit.
requirements.evidence: Build is 2 bases, 2 bins and 1 joint bolt, well under 30 parts; check_build has no errors and meshClash is clear.

finish.summary: A small two-base sewing organiser: two hex bases, each holding a two-compartment bin, joined by a joint bolt. check_build reports no errors and meshClash is clear. The only unmet item is the drawer, since the configurator would not offer a drawer position on the half bases I tried.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
